sentences.text: Erquitaia is a little-known genus of prehistoric sharks belonging to the galeomorph group.
The genus Erquitaia was first described by the scientist Henri Cappetta in 1989.
Erquitaia is classified within the class Chondrichthyes, which includes all cartilaginous fish.
It belongs to the shark superorder Galeomorphi, a group containing all modern sharks except dogfish and their relatives.
The parent group for the genus Erquitaia is Galeomorphi.
Researchers initially misidentified Erquitaia as a ray and classified it in the order Rajiformes.
Fossils of Erquitaia are found in rocks that date to the Maastrichtian stage.
